title: Lesson 34 - Virtualization scenarios: connect vs copy, OData, external data sources
description: Given a customer scenario, decide when to use virtualized data and describe virtualized data options, choosing between Salesforce Connect (OData/cross-org/custom adapters) and copying data into Salesforce for specific scenarios.

questions.question: A parent org is authoritative for Accounts and changes constantly; a subsidiary org needs to view them live in Salesforce. What is the best approach?
options: Expose the parent org's Accounts as External Objects via the cross-org adapter
questions.explanation: The cross-org adapter gives live cross-org access without copying; nightly/weekly copies (A, D) are stale and merging (C) is a bigger change than the requirement.

questions.question: Which TWO scenarios argue for COPYING rather than virtualizing?
options: Users must run approvals, validation, and fast reports on the data
The data must remain only in the source for residency
The source system is slow and the data is stable
The data changes every second and is only ever read
questions.explanation: Native automation/speed needs (A) and a slow source with stable data (C) favor copying; residency (B) and high-volatility read-only data (D) favor virtualization.

questions.question: A company needs live visibility of volatile ERP order history but Salesforce must run fast reports only on active orders. What is the best design?
options: Copy all order history into Salesforce
Copy the stable active orders and virtualize the full history via an External Object
questions.explanation: A hybrid copies the small stable/hot subset for native reporting and virtualizes the large volatile history; copying all (A) wastes storage and virtualizing the hot active orders (C) loses native speed.
